correctness.rationale: After choosing one reflection in a generating set, every other reflection may be replaced by its difference rotation; hence \(d(G)=d(A)+1\) and pair extension reduces exactly to completing prescribed rotations to a minimum generating tuple of \(A\). Such a tuple generates iff it spans every Sylow Frattini quotient, giving the stated rank inequalities for one and two prescribed rotations. Primewise counting then gives the active count and all degree strata. For divisibility, each prime-power order component of an active rotation is absorbed by the corresponding factor of \(R(a)\); in the maximal-rank case the extra factor \(p^d-p\) contributes the needed p-adic unit of valuation one because \(d\ge2\). Inactive rotations have degree zero and reflections have even degree. The packaged finite examples exercise non-elementary and mixed-Sylow branches but are not the proof.

final_claim: For \(G=\operatorname{Dih}(A)\) with \(A\) finite abelian of odd order and generator rank at least two, the entire minimum-size independence graph is determined by ranks in the Sylow Frattini quotients; this yields exact rotation/reflection degree formulas and proves that every element order divides its degree in \(\Gamma_{d(G)}(G)\).
limitations: The kernel must be finite abelian of odd order and the complement acts by inversion.
